teams.heading: Newcastle Red Bulls sign Fiji hooker Zuriel Togiatama on one-year deal
teams.body: Newcastle Red Bulls have secured the services of Fiji hooker Zuriel Togiatama on a one-year contract. The 27-year-old, who previously made 50 Super Rugby appearances for the Fijian Drua, makes the move to the Premiership ahead of the upcoming season. Newcastle head coach Dan McFarland praised the signing, noting that Togiatama is “strong in the set-piece” and will “add real quality and depth” to the club’s forward pack as they bolster their front-row options.

lead.why: The signing of a Fijian international by a top-tier Premiership club is a significant development for the national forward depth.

teams.heading: Former England prop Joe Marler confirmed as BBC’s first celebrity Gladiator
teams.body: Former England international Joe Marler is set to transition from the pitch to the studio as the first celebrity Gladiator. The 36-year-old, who previously competed in the inaugural series of Celebrity Traitors, will adopt the persona Mauler for the fourth series of the programme, which is scheduled to air in 2027. The BBC stated that the former prop will bring his characteristic "uncompromising style of play" and competitive spirit to the role when filming concludes in Sheffield.

lead.why: The transition of a high-profile former England player into mainstream entertainment is a significant news story currently dominating media coverage.

teams.heading: Ion Neculai leaves Zebre Parma to join Premiership champions Northampton Saints
teams.body: Italian international tight-head prop Ion Neculai has signed for Northampton Saints, departing Zebre Parma after 5 seasons and 51 appearances. The 25-year-old, who earned his 4th senior cap during last month's Nations Championship test against Australia, arrives at Franklin’s Gardens alongside fellow Italian Danilo Fischetti. Saints director of rugby Phil Dowson welcomed the move, identifying Neculai as a "very physical prop who enjoys the tough side of the game." Neculai officially joined his new teammates for pre-season training last week.

teams.heading: Sione Fukofuka steps down as Scotland Women head coach citing stress
teams.body: Sione Fukofuka has resigned as Scotland Women head coach to return to his family in Australia. Describing the move as the "hardest professional decision" of his life, Fukofuka cited the emotional strain of being separated from his family as the primary reason for his departure. Forwards coach Dave Butcher will assume interim control as the squad prepares for the upcoming WXV Global Series, with captain Rachel Malcolm returning to lead the 32-player group when training commences at Oriam this coming Monday.

lead.why: The departure of the head coach is the most significant development in the Scottish rugby news cycle today.

teams.heading: Wales set to re-enter world top 10 following Japan-Australia Test
teams.body: Wales are on the verge of returning to the world’s top 10 for the first time since July 2024. Despite a difficult period for the national side, Steve Tandy’s team stands to climb the rankings without playing this weekend. A defeat for Japan against Australia in Osaka would see the Brave Blossoms drop two places, moving Wales up one spot in the world standings. Just 0.04 points currently separate the two nations ahead of the upcoming fixtures.

teams.heading: Tomás Albornoz receives four-match ban for intimidating referee Angus Gardner
teams.body: Fly-half Tomás Albornoz has been suspended for four matches following a disciplinary hearing into his conduct after the defeat to England. Albornoz admitted to intimidating referee Angus Gardner after the final whistle, leading to his exclusion from this weekend’s fixture against the Springboks. The disciplinary committee acknowledged his early acceptance of the charge and a previously clear record when reducing the sanction from the six-match entry point. Santiago Carreras will start at fly-half for Argentina in his absence.

lead.why: The suspension of a key playmaker following an investigation into referee intimidation is the most significant disciplinary development.

teams.heading: Les Kiss backs inexperienced halves pair for first Wallabies Test outing
teams.body: New head coach Les Kiss has retained the halves pairing of Ryan Lonergan and Declan Meredith for his maiden match in charge against Japan. Kiss, who succeeded Joe Schmidt, has made four alterations to his starting XV, including first career starts for prop Aidan Ross and second-rower Miles Amatosero. "Every single player in the squad has pushed hard over the last fortnight to get us to this point, making selecting the matchday 23 a real challenge for the coaches," Kiss said.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones prepares Japan to face Australia at Hanazono Rugby Stadium
teams.body: Japan host Australia in Higashiosaka City this Saturday for the Lipovitan D Challenge Cup. Eddie Jones leads the Brave Blossoms against a Wallabies side beginning a new era under head coach Les Kiss. Conditions are expected to be testing, with Osaka under an excessive heat warning and potential rain forecasted. Japan, currently ranked 10th, aim to secure their first victory over the 8th-ranked Wallabies, who narrowly edged out a win in their previous meeting last October in wet conditions.

teams.body: Dave Rennie has been forced into a late change ahead of the tour opener in Cape Town, with back-rower Wallace Sititi withdrawing from the squad due to illness. teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus insists Springboks must avoid Argentina slap in the face
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has warned that focusing on the upcoming 'Greatest Rivalry' series against the All Blacks before facing Argentina would be a “slap in the face” to his opponents. The head coach has named a side featuring returning stars Eben Etzebeth, Lood de Jager, and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu for the encounter in Buenos Aires. Erasmus maintains that while he is balancing player fitness for the longer tour ahead, his squad remains fully committed to overcoming a team that previously defeated them by one point.
